title: Support diversified route and product development

blocks.text: The second supply theme covers what visitors find once they arrive: product beyond the icons, the quality of the stay and the limits of the flagship sites. All three December entries carried through as Validated.
Theme 2.2 · Product and destination capacity · Focus area 10
Support diversified route and product development

The province does not lack attractions; it lacks finished experiences around them, with assets outside the Metro left without guides, interpretation or bookable product and one touring route of six rated Ready.
**December 2025.** Support Diversified Route and Product Development (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Validated.** Idle assets and cold zones. The Infrastructure Report's spatial maps and route scorecards drove the disposition, and 11 of the 16 organisations in the stakeholder programme raised the theme. Cold zones is the report's own term; idle assets paraphrases its finding that assets are inactivated or underused.

blocks.message: Assets are spread across the province, but product, packaging and investment stop at the core routes.

blocks.text: The Infrastructure Report's own conclusion is that the constraint is less about creating new attractions and more about turning existing assets into complete, accessible visitor experiences (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p114). No deliverable counts the assets that have no product around them [assets with no bookable product or guided access, by district: needs the Wesgro supply database behind the 50,332 count].

Wesgro should deepen the three corridors closest to ready, the Garden Route, the Cape Winelands and the Overberg, and package the two outer routes as slow-travel products. The Infrastructure Report places the strongest regional opportunity in deepening existing corridors through connectivity, packaging and service depth (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p114). Dispersal needs deliberate corridor investment, not organic spillover from Cape Town (p5). Stellenbosch and George can anchor regional business events (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p41).

rows: Package bookable multi-day itineraries on each of the six touring routes, starting with the Whale Coast east of Hermanus, Route 62 and the West Coast
Activate cold-zone assets with guided tours, interpretation and bookable product, beginning with the marine and wildflower assets
Build regional conference offers in Stellenbosch and George, with stays before and after Cape Town events
Invest in accommodation and service depth beyond Hermanus, in Route 62's secondary towns and beyond Langebaan and Paternoster (focus area 15)
Refresh flagship product: Robben Island beyond the prison tour; the Cableway's lower station
Robben Island Museum; Table Mountain Aerial Cableway
Complete SA Connect rural broadband and SANParks precinct projects such as the R81.7m Agulhas lighthouse precinct

blocks.text: Chile ran Santiago, Valparaíso, the wine valleys and Patagonia as one portfolio, which raised global awareness, earned revenue in the shoulder season and lengthened stays as visitors explored several regions (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p27). The required change for the Western Cape is to sell experiences as curated journeys and move from asset marketing to experience-led packaging (p28).

**Initiative I9**, corridor product development (section 4.3). **Indicators** T1-06 share of arrivals and spend outside the Metro at impact level and T2-14 readiness by district at outcome level (section 5.2).
